items.title: Section: Four Calamities Eliminated — Even the Very Wish to Advance Further Now Recognised as a Subtle Residue

items.zh: 是諸菩薩得此忍故，得甚深住。先於第一無相住中，四種災患今悉除斷。一者、除斷於無相中有加行有功用事；二者、除斷於上清淨住精勤思慕；三者、除斷於一切種利有情事有大堪能精勤思慕；四者、除斷有微細想現在前行。是故此住名極清淨。
items.en:
Third aspect: eliminating calamities, attaining profound abiding; first, naming it. Such bodhisattvas, because of attaining this forbearance, attain profound abiding. The four calamities present back at the first markless abode are now entirely eliminated.
Second, listing them. First, eliminating the very matter of applied effort and effortful application within the markless state itself. Second, eliminating diligent yearning after a purer abode still higher. Third, eliminating diligent yearning after great capacity for benefiting every kind of sentient being. Fourth, eliminating the presently-manifesting activity of even the most subtle conceptual notion.
Third, the conclusion. This is why this abode is called utterly pure.

items.title: Section: Seven Aspects of Profundity, and the Buddha's Own Gentle Reminder Not to Abandon the Vow

items.zh: 又此菩薩於甚深住極生愛樂。即於如是法門流中，蒙諸如來覺悟勸導，授與無量引發門智神通事業。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: awakened and guided by the Buddha, bestowed with wondrous wisdom. Furthermore, such a bodhisattva, deeply delighting in this profound abiding, is, precisely within this flow of dharma, awakened and guided by the Tathāgatas, bestowed with immeasurable gateways of wisdom opening onto spiritual power and undertaking.
Commentary: Regarding "deeply delighting in this profound abiding" and the like — this profound abiding is quiescent liberation itself; this is why such a bodhisattva, within this abode, deeply delights in it. This delight flows from that same quiescent, liberated equality; this is called the flow of dharma. Precisely within this flow of dharma, the Tathāgatas, wishing to remove the obstacle to benefiting beings that arises from delighting in this state, awaken and guide such a bodhisattva, causing genuine, compassionate regard for all sentient beings not yet liberated, and bestowing the Tathāgatas' own immeasurable, wondrous wisdom. By this wisdom, every undertaking of spiritual power is drawn forth. By this undertaking, every benefit for sentient beings is accomplished.

items.title: Section: Countless Emanation-Bodies, and Tenfold Sovereignty — a Thousand Places, a Thousand Simultaneous Responses

items.zh: 如是蒙佛覺悟勸導，引發無量分身妙智。得十自在。如經廣說，應知其相。
items.en: Fifth aspect: realising the wondrous wisdom of emanation-bodies, attaining sovereignty; first, pointing to what the sutra says. Thus awakened and guided by the Buddha, such a bodhisattva draws forth immeasurable, wondrous wisdom regarding emanation-bodies, and attains tenfold sovereignty. This follows exactly as the sutra explains at length; one should understand its mark accordingly.

items.title: Section: Ten Sovereignties in Full — Life, Mind, Resources, Karma, Birth, Vow, Resolute Understanding, Wish-Fulfilment, Dharma, and Wisdom

items.zh: 得自在故，隨所欲住，如意能住；隨樂安住靜慮、解脫等諸心住，如意能住；若暫思惟一切食等諸資生具，悉皆成辦，一切世間工業明處，如其所欲悉能現行；普於一切能感生業，及於一切受生處所，皆隨所欲自在往生；隨所愛樂，一切神通所作事業皆能起作；一切妙願，隨其所欲皆得稱遂；隨於事物發起勝解，如所欲為皆成無異；隨所欲知所知境界皆如實知；普於一切名句文身得隨所欲；於一切法正安立中皆得善巧。
items.en:
Second, distinguishing sovereignty. Attaining sovereignty, one abides however one wishes, able to abide at will. Abiding in whatever meditative absorption, liberation, or mental state one delights in, able to abide at will. Whatever provisions such as food are merely thought of for even a moment, all are accomplished; every worldly craft and skilful learning manifests exactly as wished. Universally, regarding every karma producing rebirth and every place of rebirth, one takes birth exactly as wished, entirely at will. Whatever one delights in, every undertaking of spiritual power is able to be performed. Every excellent vow is fulfilled exactly as wished. Giving rise to resolute understanding regarding any matter, whatever is wished becomes exactly so, without variance. Whatever object one wishes to know is genuinely known exactly as it is. Universally, regarding every name, phrase, and letter, one obtains whatever is wished. In correctly establishing every dharma, one attains genuine skill.
Commentary: Regarding "attaining tenfold sovereignty" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: attaining sovereignty over life, mind, resources, karma, birth, vow, resolute understanding, wish-fulfilment, dharma, and wisdom — these are called the ten sovereignties.

items.title: Section: The Excellent Benefit of Sovereignty — Great Wisdom, Great Karma, and Seven Further Qualities

items.zh: 如是菩薩獲得自在，從是已去，所得自在所作勝利，廣說如經，應知其相。
items.en:
Sixth aspect: receiving the excellent benefit of attained sovereignty. Such a bodhisattva, having attained sovereignty, from this point onward receives the excellent benefit this attainment produces, exactly as the sutra explains at length; one should understand its mark accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "the excellent benefit this attainment produces" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: this bodhisattva, having attained these ten sovereignties, is at once called one of inconceivable wisdom, of immeasurable wisdom, of vast wisdom, of unbreakable wisdom, and so on at length — this bodhisattva attaining such power of wisdom, displaying every undertaking without fault in any matter. This should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Section: Never Once Departed From Seeing the Buddha — Gold Fit for a King's Own Crown, Light Rivaling a Thousand-World Brahmā

items.zh: 又能棄捨麁見諸佛，恒常無間不離見佛。其餘所有善根清淨，金喻、光喻，如經應知。
items.en:
Seventh aspect: purified wholesome roots; first, naming the cause. Furthermore, able to relinquish even the coarse beholding of the buddhas, constantly, without interruption, never once departed from seeing the buddha.
Second, pointing to the sutra's own similes. Every other purified wholesome root, the gold-simile and light-simile, should be understood exactly as the sutra explains.
Commentary: Regarding "the gold-simile and light-simile, exactly as the sutra explains" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: just as genuine gold, fashioned by a skilful goldsmith into an ornament, is fastened upon the very neck or crown of Jambudvīpa's own king, and no other treasure-ornament throughout Jambudvīpa can outshine it — so too, O sons of the buddhas, a bodhisattva abiding at this ground of immovability has wholesome roots that no hearer, solitary-realiser, nor even a seventh-ground bodhisattva can destroy. Such a bodhisattva, attaining this ground, dispels every sentient being's own dark obstruction of affliction through the great light of wisdom, by means of the very gateway of skilfully discerning wisdom. O sons of the buddhas! Just as a Mahābrahmā ruling a thousand worlds is able, in a single moment, to spread loving-kindness pervading a thousand worlds, and is also able to emit light illuminating them equally — so too, O sons of the buddhas, a bodhisattva abiding at this ground of the bodhisattva's own immovability is able to emit bodily light illuminating sentient beings across world-systems as numerous as the fine motes of dust in ten thousand myriad great trichiliocosms, gradually extinguishing every fire of affliction, bringing them to coolness.

items.title: Section: Rebirth as the Great Brahmā Ruling a Thousand Worlds, and Majestic Power Beyond All Prior Counting

items.zh: 此住菩薩受生、威力諸殊勝事，皆如經說，應知其相。
items.en:
Eighth aspect: rebirth and majestic power. This bodhisattva's own rebirth and majestic power, every excellent matter belonging to them, follow exactly as the sutra explains at length; one should understand their mark accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "every excellent matter belonging to rebirth and majestic power, exactly as the sutra explains" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: such a bodhisattva, abiding at this ground, most often becomes a great Brahmā ruling a thousand world-systems, sovereign and supreme, and so on at length. One should understand rebirth's own mark accordingly. It further says: through the power of diligence, within a single instant, such a bodhisattva attains a number of absorptions equal to the fine motes of dust in a million great trichiliocosms, and so on at length, able to transform the body into that same number of forms, and, within each and every one of those transformed bodies, able to display a retinue of bodhisattvas equal to that same number of motes of dust. One should understand majestic power's own mark accordingly.

items.title: Section: The Summary Names All Eleven Items, and Ten Names for a Single Ground — Immovable, Unturning, Hard to Attain, a Prince

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩無加行無功用無相住。謂入一切法第一義智成滿得入故；得無生法忍故；除斷一切災患故；逮得菩薩甚深住故；於法門流，蒙佛授與無量引發門智神通事業故；悟入無量分身智故；得自在故；領受所得自在勝利故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經不動地說。於此地中，捨先所有有加行、有功用道，其心昇上無加行、無功用、任運而轉不動勝道，是故此地名不動地。即由此義，當知說名無加行無功用無相住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode without applied effort, without effortful application, having no further mark — namely, because entry into every dharma's own ultimate-truth wisdom reaches complete fulfilment; because forbearance regarding the non-arising of dharmas is attained; because every calamity is eliminated; because the bodhisattva's own profound abiding is attained; because, within the flow of dharma, one is bestowed by the Buddha with immeasurable gateways of wisdom opening onto spiritual power and undertaking; because the wisdom of immeasurable emanation-bodies is realised; because sovereignty is attained; because the excellent benefit of that sovereignty is received; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of immovability.
Second, explaining. Within this ground, relinquishing every prior path involving applied effort and effortful application, the mind rises to a supreme, immovable path without applied effort, without effortful application, spontaneously turning; this is why this ground is named the ground of immovability.
Third, the correspondence. By this very meaning, one should understand this is named the abode without applied effort, without effortful application, having no further mark.

items.title: Section: The Abode of Unobstructed Understanding Opens — the Ninth Ground, Perfecting the Great Dharma-Teacher's Own Fourfold Mastery

items.en: Tenth abode, unobstructed understanding; first, the question. What is a bodhisattva's abode of unobstructed understanding?

items.title: Section: Not Yet Satisfied — Delighting in Entering a Wisdom Higher Still Than the Eighth Ground's Own Profundity

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於甚深住不生喜足，復於增上智殊勝性愛樂隨入。
items.en:
Second, the answer; first, the brief account; first, distinguishing each mark; first, delighting in entering excellent wisdom. Namely, bodhisattvas, not yet satisfied with profound abiding, further delight in entering the very excellent nature of heightened wisdom still higher.
Commentary: Regarding "the excellent nature of heightened wisdom" — the Tathāgatas' own wondrous wisdom is called heightened wisdom. The ultimate accomplishment of benefiting both oneself and others is called its excellent nature.

items.title: Section: Arousing Wisdom's Own Applied Effort to Teach Every Kind of Dharma to Every Kind of Being

items.zh: 是諸菩薩於諸法中起智加行，應為他說一切種法。
items.en: Second aspect: arousing wisdom's own applied effort to teach the dharma. Such bodhisattvas, regarding every dharma, arouse wisdom's own applied effort, and should, for the sake of others, teach every kind of dharma.

items.title: Section: Eleven Thickets of Complexity — Mastering the Mind's Own Eightfold Tangle, Affliction's Own Depths, and Karma's Ninefold Web

items.zh: 普於一切說法所作皆如實知。當知此中說法所作，謂於一切近稠林行，如此雜染、如此清淨，由此雜染、由此清淨，若所雜染、若所清淨，若非一向、若是一向、若通二種，如是一切皆如實知。
items.en:
Third aspect: genuinely knowing everything that teaching the dharma requires. Universally, regarding everything teaching the dharma requires, one genuinely knows exactly as it is. One should understand that what teaching the dharma requires means: regarding conduct approaching every kind of dense thicket, genuinely knowing what is defiled in this way, what is pure in this way, what causes this defilement, what causes this purity, what becomes defiled, what becomes purified, whether a case is not fixed one way, is fixed one way, or partakes of both — genuinely knowing all of this exactly as it is.
Commentary: Regarding "conduct approaching every kind of dense thicket" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: the thicket of mental conduct, of afflictive conduct, of karmic conduct, of faculty-conduct, of faith-conduct, of disposition-conduct, of profound-mind conduct, of latent-tendency conduct, of birth-conduct, of habituation-conduct, and of the threefold-grouping conduct — these are called every kind of conduct approaching a dense thicket.

items.title: Section: Becoming a Great Dharma-Teacher — Boundless Retention, Illustrated Through the Buddha's Own Skilful Encounter With a Proud Brahmin

items.zh: 如是菩薩，於說法中方便善巧，於說所作方便善巧，於一切種成大法師，獲得無量陀羅尼門，於一切種音詞支具剖析善巧，辯才無盡。
items.en:
Fourth aspect: becoming a great dharma-teacher; first, clarifying retentive reception. Such a bodhisattva, skilled in teaching the dharma and in every undertaking teaching requires, becomes, in every respect, a genuine great dharma-teacher, obtaining immeasurable gateways of retentive recollection, skilfully analysing every kind of sound, word, and grammatical component, eloquence inexhaustible.
Commentary: Regarding "every kind of sound, word, and grammatical component" — this refers to the buddhas' own proclaimed teaching, coherent, mutually supporting, according, clear and bright, useful, fitting, and accordant in every name, phrase, and letter it employs.

items.title: Section: Displaying True Capacity Begins — Eight Qualities of Sound Perfecting Every Word a Teacher Speaks

items.zh: 成就如是法陀羅尼領受堪能菩薩，由此勝無礙解引發言詞，能坐如是微妙法座。
items.en:
Second, displaying true capacity; first, naming it. Such a bodhisattva, having accomplished this capacity for retentive reception of the dharma's own retentive formula, is thereby able, through this excellent unobstructed understanding, to draw forth speech capable of occupying the very seat of this wondrous dharma-teaching.
Commentary: Regarding every kind of sound — coherent, mutually supporting, according, clear and bright, useful, fitting, worthy, and accordant, in every name, phrase, and letter employed — this is called every kind of sound.

items.title: Section: Closing the Fourth Aspect — Guiding, Comforting, and Settling Every Sentient Being Into Wholesome Practice

items.zh: 若於是中、若於是處宣說正法盡所有門，若由此故，於諸有情勸導、慰喻、安處事業，此等堪能皆悉成就。如是一切，廣說如經，應知其相。
items.en:
Second, listing the capacity. Within this, and in whatever place, proclaiming the true dharma exhaustively through every possible gateway; by this, guiding, comforting, and settling sentient beings into wholesome undertakings — all such capacities are genuinely accomplished.
Third, pointing onward. All of this, exactly as the sutra explains at length, should be understood accordingly.
Commentary: The Ten Grounds Sutra explains at length every function of the fourfold unobstructed understanding — with reference to specific characteristic, shared characteristic, conduct, teaching, wisdom, freedom from pride, the lesser and greater vehicles, the bodhisattva grounds, the Tathāgata's own ground, and sustaining the teaching.

items.title: Section: Gold Fit for a Wheel-Turning King's Own Crown, and Rebirth Ruling Two Thousand World-Systems

items.zh: 善根清淨、受生、威力諸殊勝事，亦廣如經，應知其相。
items.en:
Fifth aspect: purified wholesome roots, and the rest. Purified wholesome roots, rebirth, and majestic power, every excellent matter belonging to them, likewise follow exactly as the sutra explains at length; one should understand their mark accordingly.
Commentary: Regarding "purified wholesome roots, and the rest" — the Ten Grounds Sutra says: just as genuine gold, fashioned into an ornament, is fastened upon the neck or crown of a wheel-turning king himself, an ornament no lesser king's own treasure, nor any treasure of the people of the four continents, can equal — so too a bodhisattva abiding at this ground of the bodhisattva's own excellent wisdom possesses wholesome roots ever more excellent, bright, and pure, unbroken by any hearer, solitary-realiser, or lower-ground bodhisattva, and so on at length. One should understand purified wholesome roots accordingly. It further says: such a bodhisattva, abiding at this ground, most often becomes a great Brahmā of immense power, ruling two thousand world-systems, sovereign even amid sovereignty. One should understand rebirth accordingly. It further says: through the power of diligence, within a single instant, such a bodhisattva attains a number of absorptions equal to the fine motes of dust in ten incalculable hundred-thousands of buddha-lands, and so on at length, able to transform the body into that same number of forms, and, within each and every one of those transformed bodies, able to display a retinue of bodhisattvas equal to that same number of motes of dust. One should understand majestic power accordingly.

items.title: Section: The Summary Closes the Ninth Ground — This Is the Ground of Excellent Wisdom

items.zh: 當知是名略說菩薩無礙解住。謂於甚深寂靜解脫不生喜足入勝進故；於諸法中起智加行宣說法故；此所作事如實知故；得不思議大法師故；善根清淨故；受生故；威力故。若廣宣說，如十地經善慧地說。由此地中，一切有情利益安樂意樂清淨，逮得菩薩無礙解慧，由此善能宣說正法，是故此地名善慧地。即由此義，當知復名無礙解住。
items.en:
Second, closing the brief meaning. One should understand this, in brief, as the bodhisattva's abode of unobstructed understanding — namely, because, not satisfied with profound, quiescent liberation, one enters excellent advancement further; because, regarding every dharma, one arouses wisdom's own applied effort to teach the dharma; because everything this undertaking requires is genuinely known exactly as it is; because one attains the status of an inconceivable great dharma-teacher; because of purified wholesome roots; because of rebirth; because of majestic power.
Second, the broader pointer; first, pointing to it. Should one wish to hear it expounded at length, it is exactly as the Ten Grounds Sutra expounds it in its chapter on the ground of excellent wisdom.
Second, explaining. Within this ground, aspiration for benefiting and bringing ease to every sentient being becomes utterly pure, and the bodhisattva's own unobstructed understanding and wisdom are thereby attained, by which the true dharma is skilfully proclaimed; this is why this ground is named the ground of excellent wisdom.
Third, the correspondence. By this very meaning, one should understand this is also named the abode of unobstructed understanding.

blocks.text: The eighth ground's ten sovereignties, and then the ninth ground, where the bodhisattva becomes a great Dharma teacher.
Master Cháng Bǎi: yearning for the purer abode is a calamity because contrivance remains; once on the way, no need to look, just keep walking. Venerable Miào Jìng: yearning implies a little craving.
Venerable Miào Jìng: put plainly, the danger is wanting to enter nirvāṇa like an arhat. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha removes the obstacle of loving quietude and not wishing to benefit beings.
Master Cháng Bǎi: appearing in a thousand places when called from a thousand places. Sovereignty over life counters the fear of death: "a hundred years if you wish, an eon if you wish."
Venerable Miào Jìng: enabling beings to turn from ordinary to noble is the benefit.
Venerable Miào Jìng: seeing the Buddha with a grasping mind is coarse seeing; because one sees the suchness of dharmas, the seeing is unbroken.
"The mind rises to the effortless, spontaneous, immovable path." Master Cháng Bǎi: one of its names is "Prince Ground", like a śrāvaka arhat whose task is done.
Master Cháng Bǎi: not content with the eighth ground's profound abiding.
Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people do not understand their own thickets, let alone others'; the ninth-ground bodhisattva knows what helps.
Master Cháng Bǎi tells the story: a brahmin thinks, "It's as if I owe him; why does he come to my house for alms every day?" Venerable Miào Jìng: thought, but not said.
Venerable Miào Jìng: beings who do not know suffering are guided; those who know it are comforted. Like a jewelled pavilion with many doors: impermanence, suffering, emptiness.
"Pure aspiration for beings' benefit, unobstructed wisdom attained, skilled in teaching: hence Good Wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first is compassion, the second wisdom.
"Once on the way, no need to look; just keep walking." Advice for any practitioner who keeps checking how far they have come.

quiz.q: Among the four calamities removed is "diligently yearning for a purer abode." Why is even this a calamity, according to the lectures?
options: both: at the seventh, extra striving becomes a fault; yearning carries attachment and contrivance — Cháng Bǎi: once on the road, just keep walking
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: yearning for the purer abode is a calamity because contrivance remains; once on the way, no need to look — just keep walking. Venerable Miào Jìng: at the seventh ground special striving is a fault; yearning implies a little craving.

quiz.q: The eighth-ground bodhisattva "deeply delights in profound abiding" and is roused by the buddhas. How do the lectures describe the obstacle?
options: Miào Jìng: put plainly, wanting to enter nirvāṇa like an arhat — not wanting to save beings is the obstacle; Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha removes the obstacle of loving quietude over helping beings
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: put plainly, wanting to enter nirvāṇa like an arhat; not wanting to save beings is the obstacle. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha removes the obstacle of loving quietude and not wishing to benefit beings.

quiz.q: "Drawing forth wondrous wisdom of countless emanation-bodies." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: appearing wherever called — unlike ordinary people who can be in only one place
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: appearing in a thousand places when called from a thousand places — unlike ordinary people who, appearing here, can't appear elsewhere. Venerable Miào Jìng: emanation-bodies are transformation bodies.

quiz.q: The first sovereignty — "abiding however long one wishes" — is called what?
options: sovereignty over life — a hundred years or an eon, as one wishes
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a hundred years if you wish, an eon if you wish; sovereignty over life counters the fear of death. Venerable Miào Jìng: abiding ten million years at will.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say is the benefit "produced" by the sovereignties?
options: turning beings from ordinary to noble, attaining the three vehicles' paths — all merit, no fault
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: enabling beings to turn from ordinary to noble and attain the three vehicles' paths — that is the benefit; all merit, no fault.

quiz.q: "Relinquishing coarse seeing of the buddhas, never apart from seeing the Buddha." How do the lectures explain "coarse seeing"?
options: both: seeing the Buddha with grasping is coarse; the eighth ground sees suchness — seeing origination is seeing dharma and Buddha — so it's unbroken
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: seeing the Buddha with a grasping mind is coarse seeing; because one sees the suchness of dharmas, it is unbroken. Master Cháng Bǎi: first-ground bodhisattvas see coarsely, innate dharma-grasping remaining; seeing dependent origination is seeing dharma and Buddha.

quiz.q: What is the eighth abode called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra, and why?
options: Immovable — leaving effortful paths behind, the mind rises to the effortless, spontaneous, immovable path
quiz.why: "Leaving the effortful path behind, the mind rises to the effortless, spontaneous, immovable path — hence the Immovable Ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: spontaneous means natural, no effort needed.

quiz.q: Among the eighth ground's names is "Prince Ground." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: free of household faults and afflictions — like an arhat, task completed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the fourth name is "Prince Ground" — without the faults of household life, without afflictions; comparable to the śrāvaka arhat whose task is done.

quiz.q: The ninth-ground bodhisattva, not satisfied, delights in "heightened wisdom." What is it?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the Tathāgata's wondrous wisdom is "heightened wisdom"; not content with the eighth ground's profound abiding. Venerable Miào Jìng: though the state is high, still not satisfied.

quiz.q: "Conduct approaching every dense thicket — all known as it is." How do the lectures explain "thicket conduct"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people don't know their own thickets — teaching is shooting in the dark, but the ninth ground knows; Miào Jìng: 行 is the mind, 近 "attached" — sometimes pure, sometimes careless
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people don't understand their own thickets, let alone others'; their teaching is shooting in the dark, but the ninth-ground bodhisattva knows what helps. Venerable Miào Jìng: 行 is the mind; 近 means attached — sometimes I'm pure and proper, sometimes careless.

quiz.q: Discussing the great dharma-teacher, both lectures tell of a brahmin and an alms-seeking monk. How did the brahmin feel?
options: both: the brahmin felt as if he owed the monk a debt — coming every day for alms
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "It's as if I owe him — why does he come to my house for alms every day?"; one should offer before the teaching, since dharma is precious, not for sale. Venerable Miào Jìng: as if he owed a debt — thought but not said. The English note's "struck with shame" isn't in the lectures.

quiz.q: "Guiding, comforting, and settling beings." How do the lectures distinguish guiding and comforting?
options: Miào Jìng: for those unaware of suffering, guiding; for those aware, comforting; Cháng Bǎi: guiding them from faults to good, comforting those who know suffering so they keep practising
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: beings who don't know suffering are guided; those who know it are comforted. Master Cháng Bǎi: guiding beings to abandon faults and turn to good; comforting those who know suffering so they keep cultivating good.

quiz.q: What is the ninth abode called in the Ten Grounds Sūtra, and why?
options: Good Wisdom — pure aspiration to benefit beings, unobstructed wisdom, skill in teaching
quiz.why: "Pure aspiration for beings' benefit, unobstructed wisdom attained, skilled in teaching — hence Good Wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first is compassion, the second wisdom.
